paragraphs_in_document_order: Plan the day out P6
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
White paper version | Same task and finish | Point, speak, draw, write or use a scribe.
P6 | Supported | Team ____ | My code ____
PRACTICE COSTS ONLY. Ten pupils and four adults. No quote or payment. Use the cost cards. Owner handwritten venue name: ____________________.
1 Use the common total £364. Choose a practice transport card with an adult. Add its return cost.
2 Find 10% by dividing that total by 10. Add this extra amount. Use a calculator or ask for one step at a time.
3 Divide the plan total by 10 pupil places. Say or point to your cost and a reason for the team choice.
Common cost: pupil entry £150 + adult entry £80 + lunch/drink £84 + pupil shop reserve £50 = £364.
Return transport: existing minibus £150; hired minibus £450; hired coach £650. Owner must check capacity, access, drivers and all costs.
My check: £364 + transport £____ = £____.10% contingency £____. Plan total £____.Divide by 10 pupil places = £____ each. This is a cost share, not a charge to families.
Shop: up to £5 per pupil. Buying nothing is valid. Spend £____; money left £____. Adult shopping is outside this model.
Finish

Give one checked cost and one team budget line: “We choose ____ because ____. Total £____, or £____ per pupil place. We still need to check ____.” Show, say or share quietly. Keep your own calculation even if you visit station D.

resources.title: Station support one
paragraphs_in_document_order: Station support one
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Set up

P5: support mixed team A. Put out role cards, the three route sheets, an approved extract and pencils. P6: support team A with the cost cards and a calculator if useful. The teacher introduces and leads both shared tasks. Offer white, blue or pink paper with the same words and finish.
What to do

P5: help pupils choose what they want to see at the open-air museum, form a then and now question and assign shared roles. P6: help the team include ten pupils and four adults, compare transport totals and add ten per cent to the whole planning total. Keep the shop reserve clear; spending nothing is valid.
What to look for

Look for a choice linked to an extract, a question the exhibit could answer, a fair role and a checked calculation. Keep one home pupil at the team while short appointments take place. Help returning pupils rejoin the cost check.
What to record
Use anonymous codes. Keep one actual action or exact scribed sentence, the work or photo reference and actual help. Do not fill in success before it happens. Award masks remain [AWARD] and [QUAL].
Prompt and finish

Point; ask a short question; rephrase; offer a frame or choice; model the first step only, then return the task. No cold calling. A pupil may pass, point or answer privately. Finish: P5 plan and optional pitch; P6 checked cost and one-line budget pitch. No heat or food activity.

resources.title: Station support two
paragraphs_in_document_order: Station support two
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Set up

Support team B in P5 and P6. Put out role cards, route sheets, approved extracts and pencils. Have the cost cards and a calculator ready for P6. The teacher gives the goal and leads each task. Paper colour is a choice, not a level.
What to do

P5: help pupils compare then and now, choose a focus and plan one object sketch with a caption. Keep an extract code or an unanswered question beside the claim. P6: check the group subtotal, add one transport option, then add ten per cent to that whole total. Divide the final planning total by ten pupil places.
What to look for

Check that all fourteen travellers appear in relevant costs. A shop reserve is money kept available, not money that must be spent. A per-pupil planning figure does not set a family charge. Keep at least one home pupil at each team during appointments and help returners check their own cost line.
What to record

Keep anonymous codes, one observed action or exact scribed line, a coded work or photo reference and actual support. Keep errors and the learner's own correction visible. Do not infer independent work from a team answer.
Prompt and finish

Point; ask a short question; rephrase; offer a frame or choice; model one first step and return the task. No cold calling; allow pass, point or private response. Finish: one team plan, then a checked budget pitch. Only paper research and modelling; no heat or food activity.

Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Set up

P5: support mixed team C with the same planning task. P6: move to station D with the accepted Lesson 6 materials, id grow_community_cakesale_a2w1. These materials are referenced, not rebuilt or reproduced here. The teacher leads the shared goals and supports team C during P6.
Calendar and appointments

The current session is Thursday 12 November 2026. This order supersedes the earlier calendar attached to GCS-2_SEGMENT_D; it does not alter the accepted lesson content. Use short GROW appointments from 13:40 to 13:48 and 13:49 to 13:57. Keep at least one home pupil in each team. Return pupils promptly to their team cost check. Adjust the appointment order if a home team would empty.
What to look for

Support the existing Lesson 6 decisions only. Point to the accepted task and use its support route. Retain the learner's actual choice, reason and help. Do not introduce a second new task, food handling or heat. Do not claim that Lesson 6 or an award is complete.
What to record

Use the accepted evidence route and anonymous codes. Note the actual decision or pending check and actual support. Add only an authentic action to the Local Choice evidence line; keep [AWARD] and [QUAL] masked.
Prompt and finish

Point; short question; rephrase; frame or choice; model the first step only, then return the task. No cold calling. Allow pass or private response. Finish: an existing decision recorded or left pending, then return to the team budget pitch.

resources.title: Then and now enquiry cards
paragraphs_in_document_order: Then and now enquiry cards
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
How to use these cards

These are made-up comparison models for practice. They do not describe the open-air museum or promise what is there. Read an owner-approved extract to research the real visit. Ask an adult to read or scribe if useful. No cold calling. You may pass, point or share privately.
Money then and now

MODEL: One stall takes cash. Another stall takes cash or a card. A buyer still checks the price and chooses what to buy. Buying nothing is a valid choice.CHECK QUESTION: How did a buyer pay, and what could they buy? What evidence would show this?Owner-approved extract or object code: __________What it shows: __________  What is still unknown: __________
Work and industry

MODEL: One worker shapes a part by hand. In another model, a machine shapes it. A worker checks the result in both. A tool can change some parts of a job.CHECK QUESTION: Which task changed, and what skill did the worker still need?Owner-approved extract or object code: __________What it shows: __________  What is still unknown: __________
Then and now enquiry cards continued
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Home life

MODEL: One home uses a stove to heat water. Another uses a switch. In both models, someone checks the water is safe to use. We only read and sketch these models; we do not heat water or use food.CHECK QUESTION: How did a daily task change, and who did the work?Owner-approved extract or object code: __________What it shows: __________  What is still unknown: __________
Our tabletop exhibit plan

1. Choose one enquiry theme and one question.2. Make one object sketch or plan which object to sketch.3. Add a short THEN caption and a short NOW caption.4. Keep an approved extract or object code beside each claim, or mark the question unanswered.FINISH: one sketch, then and now captions, and a source code or open question. A neat display does not prove a claim.
Our visit choice

At the open-air museum, we want to find out ______ because ______. We need an adult to check whether this is available.Owner to fill by hand only: ____________________Our team question is ______. Our job pairs are ______. We can pitch our idea, ask an adult to read it with permission, or show it privately.

resources.title: Trip cost challenge cards
paragraphs_in_document_order: Trip cost challenge cards
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Planning allowances

Use these proposal allowances for the task. They are planning figures, not confirmed prices or a request for payment. The group has ten pupils and four adults: fourteen travellers. The visit is to the open-air museum.Owner to fill by hand only: ____________________
The shared costs

Pupil entry: 10 × £15 = £150.Adult entry: 4 × £20 = £80.Lunch and drink: 14 × £6 = £84.Pupil shop reserve: 10 × £5 = £50.Shared subtotal: £150 + £80 + £84 + £50 = £364.The shop reserve is money kept available. Each pupil can spend £0 to £5. Buying nothing is valid. No adult shop spending is included.
Transport options

Option A planning allowance: £150.Option B planning allowance: £450.Option C planning allowance: £650.These are whole-group transport figures. Add one option once. An adult must check the return journey, capacity for fourteen travellers, access and the actual quote. No transport is booked or confirmed by this task.
The order of the check

1. Start with £364.2. Add one transport option.3. Find ten per cent of that whole planning total.4. Add that ten per cent as a reserve.5. Divide the final total by ten pupil places.FINISH: a checked total and one-line team budget pitch.
Trip cost challenge cards continued
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Staff check figures

Option A: £364 + £150 = £514. Ten per cent is £51.40. Final total £565.40. Per pupil place: £565.40 ÷ 10 = £56.54.Option B: £364 + £450 = £814. Ten per cent is £81.40. Final total £895.40. Per pupil place: £895.40 ÷ 10 = £89.54.Option C: £364 + £650 = £1,014. Ten per cent is £101.40. Final total £1,115.40. Per pupil place: £1,115.40 ÷ 10 = £111.54.
Aspire comparison

An optional comparison divides by fourteen travellers instead. It answers a different question. Rounded to the nearest penny: A £40.39; B £63.96; C £79.67 per traveller. Label this comparison clearly. Keep the required per-pupil-place answer divided by ten. Neither figure sets a family charge.
Buying nothing

A pupil can choose to spend £0 while the plan still holds the £5 reserve. If the whole group removes all ten shop reserves before the ten per cent check, subtract £50 first. New final totals are A £510.40; B £840.40; C £1,060.40. Keep the chosen assumption clear and recalculate the reserve.
Our pitch and open checks

We propose option __. With the shop reserve, our checked total is £__. The planning cost per pupil place is £__. We still need an adult to check __.Keep actual prices, permission, booking and any funding decision unconfirmed until the adult checks them. No cold calling; show the line, pass or share privately.

shape_text.text: Real cost, access and capacity checks stay with the owner.

shape_text.name: credit
shape_text.text: Made by Matt · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale

slides.notes:
One minute, 12:58–12:59. These practice allowances come from Proposal 1, updated for ten pupils and four supervising adults. Pupil entry 10 × £15 = £150. Adult entry 4 × £20 = £80. Lunch and drink 14 × £6 = £84. Optional pupil shop reserve 10 × £5 = £50, adult shopping excluded. Common cost £364. Return transport allowances are £150 existing minibus, £450 hired minibus with driver and £650 hired coach with driver. Totals before contingency are £514, £814 and £1014. Add ten per cent: £51.40, £81.40 and £101.40. Planning totals are £565.40, £895.40 and £1115.40. Funding share per pupil place if all adult costs are allocated across ten pupils is £56.54, £89.54 and £111.54; this is a model allocation, not a charge. The worksheets also distinguish cost per traveller across fourteen people. Buying nothing means actual shop spending can be zero and unused reserve remains unspent. Verify real admission, concessions, access, capacity, return quote and food arrangements separately. Hired driver cost is included in the practice transport allowance; the model does not add that driver’s entry or lunch. An adult driving an existing vehicle cannot supervise pupils while driving. No booking, payment, publication or external contact is performed.

Stop tools, return materials, place team work in the labelled tray, clear hands and the work surface as needed, take a calm seated reset and listen to the teacher’s next instruction. Keep access routes clear. The teacher leads every task. Three TAs support hands-on. During P6, the teacher coordinates the three team cost tasks while one TA runs the accepted Lesson 6 decision station in short slots; other TAs support the shared task. Follow the owner run-sheet for the exact station and withdrawal arrangement. At 14:00 record one individual evidence line for each code P01 to P10, with a permitted photo reference or drawing/observation alternative, the pupil’s own sentence or exact scribed words and actual support. A group photograph alone does not prove every pupil’s contribution. Keep actual outcomes blank until observed. Use the usual award masks. Keep the learner’s idea, adult reply, one next-step prompt and response in the same colour, on the same page, or usual mode before recording R; record E only for actual banking.
